guarantees.claim: For each share j (0..Share-1) and each slice i (0..DInEntry-1), storage_d[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth] is set to storage[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth] ^ data_i[j] when addr_i == i[DInAddr-1:0], otherwise to storage[j][i*DInWidth+:DInWidth].
guarantees.cond: always_comb block active (xor_message compile-time true); for all j, i

assumptions.claim: The total width of each storage share is an integer multiple of DInWidth, so that all bits are covered by the DInEntry slices.
assumptions.risk: If violated, slice indexing may exceed array bounds or leave some bits of storage_d unassigned, causing mismatch between storage and storage_d or synthesis errors.

assumptions.claim: data_i[j] has bit width exactly equal to DInWidth.
assumptions.cond: when xor_message is true and the block is active
assumptions.risk: Width mismatch can cause elaboration error or unintended truncation/extension, corrupting the XOR operation.

assumptions.claim: addr_i, when compared to i[DInAddr-1:0], refers to a valid slice index within the storage address space; any upper bits of addr_i beyond DInAddr are assumed harmless or zero.
assumptions.cond: when the block is active and the loops execute
assumptions.risk: Incorrect alias (e.g., upper bits set) could cause XOR update at an unintended slice, potentially corrupting the digest state.

uncertain_points.claim: The assignment storage_d = keccak_out on line 485 is dead code when xor_message is true and the for-loops cover all bits of storage_d (guaranteed by A1). The block only exists when xor_message is true, so keccak_out never appears in the final value of storage_d within this block.
uncertain_points.cond: xor_message compile-time true, loops cover entire width
uncertain_points.risk: If the assertion A1 were bypassed and DInEntry*DInWidth did not equal the state width, leftover bits would be driven by keccak_out, mixing round output with state and causing a cryptographic fault. Under the assertion, the dead assignment only obscures design intent.
